findings.F1: Etymology falsely derives although from Latin alter through French; it is all + though.
findings.F2: Synonym discrimination reverses register: though is more informal and spoken, although more formal.
findings.F3: Sense 1 example 'Although she was tired, but she stayed up to help.' is ungrammatical.
findings.F4: The rule against although plus but is stated in three fields (explanation, adaptation note, learner error).
findings.F5: The but compare note says 'in the other order' but its example keeps the same order; misleading.
findings.F6: if-conj in sense 1 compare is not a confusable of although.
findings.F7: when-conj in sense 1 compare is not a confusable of although.
findings.F8: The even-though 'stronger contrast' fact is stated in both the compare note and synonym discrimination.
findings.F9: Learner-error note says although is never followed by a noun alone; reduced 'although a doctor' is grammatical.
findings.F10: despite-prep is listed both in sense 1 compare and in see_also.
